newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The Post Office plans heavy cost containment and marketing exercises while focusing on improving operating efficiencies in a bid to boost performance, managing director Frank Touwen said.

- More than six billion rand in mortgage loans has been facilitated for previously excluded areas by the Mortgage Indemnity Fund since its creation in 1995. The fund is intended to encourage bank lending into the low-cost housing market.
- The Democratic Party would not participate in the government of national unity because this might lead to a "muzzling" of the party's role as a vigorous opposition, party leader Tony Leon said.
- South African pet owners forked out more than one billion rand to feed, care for and pamper their animals last year.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Organised labour has demanded tough action against companies involved in bypassing customs laws, and so robbing the country of millions of rand in revenue.
- Exchange controls may be unconstitutional, according to a study by economists at Absa, the country's second-largest banking group.
- Black empowerment group Brimstone Investments said it would raise 138 million rand to finance acquisitions, including a three percent stake in Norwich Holdings.
SAKE-BEELD
- The restructuring and partial privatisation of Telkom took a great step forward at the weekend when the government reached agreement in principle with trade unions on the process of approval.
- Negotiations have begun on a bill on minimum service standards.
- The government is appointing a special task group to cut red tape in the small business sector.
THE STAR
- Police are alarmed by an internal memorandum restricting the use of firearms or force when arresting suspects.
- Orlando Pirates soccer coach Augusto Palacios had to be escorted by police from a stadium in Springs as unruly fans went on the rampage after his team lost.
- Municipal authorities in southern Johannesburg and the central business district are taking tough action against defaulters who have not paid electricity and water bills.
